issues.description: Function return type mismatch for fix_fix2float: the function fix_fix2float is declared/defined with different return types across repository artifacts. In template_repository/example_program/src/math_fix.h it is declared as "float fix_fix2float(fix_t f);" (line 40), while in template_repository/tests/src/math_fix.h it is defined as "double fix_fix2float(fix_t f)" (line 31). The solution repository uses "float" consistently in both example_program and tests. This inconsistency creates an ABI/signature mismatch between translation units (test code vs example program code) and can produce incorrect results or runtime failures when code compiled with differing declarations is linked together. Students running or linking tests against their implementations may observe failing tests or undefined behavior because callers and callee disagree on the return type.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the return type of fix_fix2float across all artifacts. Prefer the project-wide use of float (to match the solution). Change the definition in template_repository/tests/src/math_fix.h from returning double to returning float, and ensure the declaration/definition in example_program/src/math_fix.h and any other headers/implementations use the same type. Verify and, if necessary, update call sites and printf/format usage so types match (e.g. %f expects double for varargs but float return values will be promoted when passed through variadic functions; still ensure prototypes are identical across translation units). After changes, rebuild tests and example program to confirm consistent ABI and correct behavior.
